searchText: I noticed that "light" call failures also return `EXTCALL_REVERT`. are we should about it? Don't we want the "revert" to be only for "user programmable errors"? IIRC it has been decided like this on one of the EOF calls, can't tell offhand the specific rationale, or when that was. I think it was because of some edge cases in gas introspection Like somehow if you get the other failure code, you can find out if you are at the end of the call stack or not I think rationale was REVERT doesn't consume all gas, similar to light failures **EOF Implementers Call #49** Meeting Info: June 05, 2024 , 15:00 UTC Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1055 Recording Playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLJqWcTqh_zKHu7Z91YVYWy_PSmOc_66-F Zoom: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/88940506383?pwd=aTdsbHVyMTNDSUFHYmhTWlI2ZEVldz09 I made finally some simple execution benchmark for simple swap function on evmone. It's added to the doc I shared earlier https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/solidity_eof_poc Added to EOF Meeting Agenda's Resources. I'm trying to figure out why is evmone complaining about this test: It was passing on a previous commit, this is the only failing test for the set of tests in the main branch of EEST I think they started enforcing initcode and runtime code sizes in validation It's generated based on this test: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/blob/e80addbb8f1c973433bbf73158f801b312eedc58/tests/prague/eip7692_eof_v1/eip7620_eof_create/test_eofcreate_failures.py#L171 but there is no data in either of the containers (I think) It's the size of the top level container? It's > 0xFFFF Right... it's the subcontainers I was testing here... It's the total size of the subcontainer, cranked up to 64k. All code no data. This blurs the line of testing what is possible and what is legal on mainnet. The EOFCREATE call should fail as initcode > 48k and the returncontract call should also fail as deployed contract size > 24k. Should it be enforced in container validation or at runtime? Perhaps we should disable those tests for a week or two. The ones greater than inticode and runtimecode size. I think we should not really add something to the pre that is impossible to deploy, we have some very specific scenarios to e.g. test for collisions but we are very careful when we write these But in this specific case, how is evmone even able to detect it comes from an impossible initcontainer? Or does it simply check for the container to be < 64k? I think we should not allow anything > 24k in the pre, but I don’t really know if this is the case for existing tests tbh
